method: Unicorn execution of the vendor port-event handler and of three excerpts of Mixer::Process (input gather, output gather, output dispatch) with buffers replaced by recognisable pointers and processors replaced by recording vtables; static instruction checks for the bridge, active-mask source, registration loop and queued job.
findings: Source IDs 12-15 and 22-25 share internal slots 22-29, which the gather fills from JUCEJack in_13..in_20 when those channels are active; the port-event handler connects usb1in:capture_3..10 to exactly those ports. These are four physical stereo pairs, not eight independent paths: IDs 12/22, 13/23, 14/24, 15/25 alias.

Slots 30-37 (IDs 26-29) are in_21..in_28 (usb1in:capture_11..18). Slots 12-13 (ID 11, SMART Pads) are two mixer-internal buffer channels (object mixer+0xc73c8, channel-table pointer at +0x10), never a JACK port.

JUCEJack out_15/16 (usb1out:playback_1/2) and out_19/20 (usb2out:playback_1/2) are written inside Mixer::Process, before it returns, by the processor members at mixer+0xc2080 and mixer+0xc2090; the queued job only writes the monitor outputs. Inactive (unconnected) outputs receive a mixer scratch buffer instead. In raw-strip multitrack mode, the first source strip is copied to out_15/16 instead of the main mix processor running: the port is still callback-owned, but its audio is not the stereo main mix in that mode. The synchronous Chat output processor dispatch is also skipped in that branch; Secondary continues to be dispatched.
The active channel masks are rebuilt from jack_port_connected: an unconnected port is neither requested from jackd nor processed by the mixer in that period, so a path bound to it stays unobserved.
limitations: The bridge consumes up to 36 input / 46 output bits; the engine construction of the channel-name arrays passed to JACK device open was not located. Sequential registration of old catalog in_35/36 implies registration of in_13..20 whenever the old plan successfully binds. Old out_18 does not by itself prove out_19/20 exists. The native pipeline requires every plan port registered before it can attach; absent new ports would prevent the whole pipeline from attaching, not merely skip those paths. Live port counts and USB-mode startup tests remain separate evidence.

Both raw-strip and table-copy multitrack branches are emulated with synthetic active masks; the writer of the mask at mixer+0xc7d48 and its relationship to GUI multitrack mode settings were not located.
Fixtures stub buffer constructors, processors, allocation, printf and memcpy; PAC/BTI hints are skipped.
No device was flashed, probed or used for audio; live port snapshots are separate evidence.
